text: mean right now somewhere a person is about to sign for a five hundred thousand dollar house
the bank said yes the agent is smiling every one is calling it a smart move and the math says that within a year this person could be one broken water heater away from panic
so who can actually afford this house not who gets approved who can afford it and still sleep at night
the answer is a much smaller group than you think and the last group on this list is the one almost nobody talks about
first a truth most buyers never hear a bank approving you and you affording the house are two different questions
the bank asks will this loan probably get paid back you need to ask can i still have a life while paying it
those two answers can be miles apart let's start with the price
a five hundred thousand dollar house is about six times the yearly income of a household earning eighty five thousand
six times hold on to that ratio because everything else builds on it
now the down payment the classic goal is twenty per cent on this house that is a hundred thousand in cash
if you save ten per cent of an eighty five thousand income which is already a strong habit
you put away about eighty five hundred a year at that speed the down payment takes around twelve years and that is if prices stand still
they rarely do so most buyers put down less say ten per cent which is fifty thousand that feels like a relief but it comes with a hidden cost mortgage insurance
it is a monthly fee that protects the lender not you because you put less money down
it can run a few hundred a month now the loan itself fifty thousand down leaves four hundred fifty thousand to borrow at an inch's rate around six and a half per cent over thirty years
the payment on the loan alone is about twenty eight hundred and fifty a month and that is just the loan the house still has to be owned
add property taxes in many places that is around five hundred a month
home insurance around three hundred and rising in areas with floods fires or storms
mortgage insurance round two fifty and then maintenance the bill everyone forgets until a pipe bursts at night a common rule is to set aside one per cent of the home's value every year
that is five thousand or about four hundred seventeen a month add it all up
twenty eight fifty plus five hundred plus three hundred plus two fifty plus four seventeen
about forty three hundred a month for one house with nothing broken yet
so what income does that take a popular rule says housing should stay under twenty eight per cent of your gross income
at that level forty three hundred a month needs an income of about one hundred eighty five thousand a year
lenders often allow more but that is their limit not your comfort's own even if you stretch to thirty five per cent you still need a round one hundred fifty thousand
remember that range one hundred fifty to one hundred eighty five thousand now ask how many households earn that
it is a minority which means for a large part of the population this house is not a goal
it is a stretch wearing a nice suit but what about people earning well
let's test it meet a couple with a combined income of one hundred sixty thousand
that sounds comfortable after taxes and deductions say they take home nine thousand five hundred a month
housing takes forty three hundred that leaves about fifty two hundred now add real life
two car payments eight hundred car insurance two fifty fuel three hundred
student loans six hundred health costs four hundred groceries eight hundred utilities and phones four fifty
that is thirty six hundred what remains but sixteen hundred for clothes kids medical bills repairs holidays retirement emergency savings and any kind of fun
houseing is eating nearly half of their take home pay and they are not reckless
no luxury trips no expensive toys they simply bought what the market calls normal
now watch the year unfold month four the carnes breaks
eight hundred on to a credit card once seven the air conditioning dice
thirty five hundred financed month nine when partner's hours get cut and suddenly they are short every single month
and the emergency fund it never got built because there was never anything left to build it with
that is the moment a home stops feeling like security and starts feeling like pressure
so the question returns who can actually afford this house let's go through the three groups that really can
the first group is the high stable earners households that clear the income range we calculated with room to spare and whose jobs are not fragile
not just high income but income that survives a bad year the second group is the buyers with a big down payment
maybe from years of saving maybe from family help maybe from selling an earlier home that grew in value
a bigger down payment shrinks the loan the interest and the mortgage insurance all at once
it changes the entire math but it is also the group that already had a head start
and the third group is the one i promised the low cost lifers
people with almost no other debt one car or none small fixed expenses and a calm life style
their income may be average but their monthly pressure is low so the house fits inside a very lean life
that is possible but it is a lifetile choice not a casual purchase
and one big surprise can still shake it notice what is missing
the average household stretching to make it work that is the group the market quietly invites and the group that carries the most risk
so before you fall in love with any listing run a simple stress test
question one if one income disappeared for three months could you still cover the full housing cost
question two if a five thousand dollars surprise arrived to morrow could you pay it without borrowing
question three after all bills can you still invest or save every month
if the answer to any of these is no the house is bigger than your life
and there is no shame in that answer it just means you have options you can look at a lower price
you can keep renting and invest the difference you can wait and build a larger down payment first
you can look at a cheaper area or a smaller home the goal is not to own the biggest house
the goal is to own a house that leaves room for you because real wealth is not equity you cannot touch
real wealth is margin it is the freedom to fix the roof and still contribute to your future
it is sleeping without doing mental math at two in the morning so run your own numbers
conclude every cost be honest about how stable your income is and remember the bank's risk limit is not your life limit
this biddo was for education and general information only your numbers rates and taxes will differ

so calculate your own situation before making any decision if this change how you see housing watch the next fidio because there is one cost hidden inside every home purchase that almost nobody includes in their budget
and it can quietly be worth tens of thousands
